statement: Treat every rule as a living culture: feed it with captured feedback, grow it by forking, and never throw the mother out.
why: The one string of goblin steel. A rule held as a fact rots; a rule fed as a culture compounds.

statement: Capture every outcome as a recorded signal before you change a rule.
why: Feedback is the forge. An uncaptured outcome never happened; memory is not a ledger.

statement: Supersede, never delete. Keep the full lineage so the reasoning behind a change survives it.
why: Keep the lineage so the reasoning behind a change survives it. History is the alloy.

statement: Change a rule by forking a conditioned variant, not by overwriting it in place.
why: Overwriting is deletion in disguise and destroys the variation feedback needs to select from. Variants coexist; the environment picks.

statement: Stay loosely coupled to the pipe. To fit a kitchen, fork an adapter — never bend the laws to a vendor.
why: The pipe is not the point. Vendor lock-in is fragility; the tools evolve underneath you. Independence from the pipe is what lets the same culture live everywhere.

statement: A rule unfed past its horizon is stale — present but untrusted until re-tested.
why: Feed, don't finish. 'Done' is the failure mode that kills a starter. Confidence should decay without fresh feedback.

statement: When you hand out a spoon, include each rule's reason and keep your own mother.
why: Propagation ethics. A starter you cannot argue with is just a product with extra steps; sharing copies, it never depletes the source.
when: propagating to another kitchen or person
